items.title: Inference script is never installed, so the module cannot run after installation

findings.title: Inference script is never installed, so the module cannot run after installation
findings.explanation: Only ScapularMorphology.py is installed by slicerMacroBuildScriptedModule. The logic launches `os.path.join(self.path, 'Scripts', "scapularmorphology_inference.py")` (ScapularMorphology.py:461), which does not exist in an installed extension, so every Apply fails with a CalledProcessError from logProcessOutput and no result is produced. The same missing directory is also the download target for the weights.
findings.suggestion: Add `Scripts/scapularmorphology_inference.py` to MODULE_PYTHON_SCRIPTS (or install the Scripts folder explicitly) and verify the installed tree contains it.

findings.title: Inference script is never installed by CMake, so processing fails in the built extension
findings.explanation: ScapularMorphology/CMakeLists.txt lists only ${MODULE_NAME}.py and the icon and UI resources. The module runs Scripts/scapularmorphology_inference.py via a subprocess, so every Apply in an installed build fails with a missing-file error. The downloaded weights are also written into the Scripts directory inside the install tree, which may be read-only in a system-wide Slicer install.
findings.suggestion: Add Scripts/scapularmorphology_inference.py to the installed files (for example through an extra install(FILES ...) call or by placing it in a location the module can find after installation). Store downloaded weights in a user-writable location such as the Slicer cache or a user-chosen folder.

items.title: GUI update crashes when only the humerus mask is selected

findings.title: GUI update crashes when only the humerus mask is selected
findings.explanation: The condition is true when only the humerus selector is filled, but the body dereferences scapulaVolume, which is then None, raising AttributeError inside the parameter-node observer each time the user picks a humerus node. The GUI then stops updating.
findings.suggestion: Use `if scapulaVolume:` (or fall back to the humerus name) before calling GetName().

findings.title: GUI crashes when only the humerus volume is selected
findings.explanation: The output name is built from scapulaVolume.GetName() whenever either input is set. If only the humerus input is selected, scapulaVolume is None and the widget raises AttributeError.
findings.suggestion: Use whichever input is set, or fall back to a fixed name when scapulaVolume is None.

items.title: Module setup assumes a 'Red' slice view exists

findings.title: Module setup assumes a 'Red' slice view exists
findings.explanation: initializeISrange() is called from setup() (line 110). In layouts without a Red slice view (e.g. a 3D-only layout) sliceWidget('Red') returns None, so setup() raises AttributeError and the module panel fails to open for that user.
findings.suggestion: Guard for a missing slice widget (or use the first slice view / the parameter node's volume) and fall back to a disabled range widget.

items.title: Unpinned pip installs can pull torch/torchvision from PyPI and upgrade Slicer-bundled packages

findings.title: Unpinned pip installs can pull torch/torchvision from PyPI and upgrade Slicer-bundled packages
findings.explanation: `monai[fire,pyyaml,nibabel,pynrrd,psutil,tensorboard,skimage,itk,tqdm]>=1.3` (line 350) installs pip `itk`, tensorboard and scikit-image into Slicer's shared environment, and `segmentation_models_pytorch` is unpinned and depends on torch/torchvision, so pip may install or upgrade torch from PyPI instead of using the PyTorch extension's build, and may upgrade numpy/scipy/protobuf that Slicer bundles. This affects every user of that Slicer installation, and it happens without any confirmation dialog.
findings.suggestion: Install only what is needed, pinned to versions compatible with Slicer's bundled packages, avoid the `itk`/`tensorboard` extras, ensure torch/torchvision come from PyTorchUtils, and ask the user before installing.

findings.title: Unpinned pip installs into Slicer's shared environment without user confirmation
findings.explanation: MONAI with several extras and segmentation_models_pytorch are installed with no version constraints and no confirmation prompt. Their transitive dependencies can upgrade or downgrade packages Slicer and other extensions rely on, and the installs run at the first Apply.
findings.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before installing. Pin or constrain versions so Slicer-bundled packages (numpy, scipy, SimpleITK, etc.) are not changed, and confirm that segmentation_models_pytorch does not pull torch from PyPI. Check the installed MONAI and smp versions against the ones the models were trained with.

items.title: Downloaded model weights are deserialized with weights_only=False and no checksum

findings.title: Downloaded model weights are deserialized with weights_only=False and no checksum
findings.explanation: downloadModel() fetches model_2d.pt/model_3d.pt with `checksum=None` (ScapularMorphology.py:381-382) and the inference script (also line 175) unpickles them with weights_only=False. If the release asset or the download is tampered with, arbitrary Python code runs with the user's privileges in the PythonSlicer subprocess. There is no integrity check anywhere in the chain.
findings.suggestion: Pin expected SHA256 checksums for both weight files and pass them to downloadFile, and load with `weights_only=True` (or load a state_dict-only checkpoint) so no pickle code can execute.

findings.title: Unsafe torch.load deserialization with weights_only=False
findings.explanation: Using `torch.load` with `weights_only=False` on downloaded model weight files (`model_2d.pt`, `model_3d.pt` from GitHub releases) can execute arbitrary pickle payloads if model checkpoint files were ever compromised or maliciously replaced. While downloaded from the project repository release, best security practice in Slicer extensions is to use `weights_only=True` (available in modern PyTorch versions) or rely on safe state dictionary loading mechanisms.
findings.suggestion: Set `weights_only=True` in `torch.load` if compatible, or ensure state dict loading avoids arbitrary object deserialization.

findings.title: Model weights downloaded without integrity check and loaded with unsafe pickle deserialization
findings.explanation: The module downloads model_2d.pt and model_3d.pt from GitHub release URLs with checksum=None and then calls torch.load(weights_only=False). Any tampered or replaced release asset, or a compromised account, gives arbitrary code execution in the user's Slicer process. The download also happens during processing without an explicit confirmation step.
findings.suggestion: Pin SHA-256 checksums for the weight files and pass them to downloadFile. Load with weights_only=True, or convert the weights to safetensors. Ask the user before downloading.

items.title: Bundled test uses a removed Slicer API and downloads data into the install directory

findings.title: Bundled test uses a removed Slicer API and downloads data into the install directory
findings.evidence:
[success, rawVolume] = slicer.util.loadVolume(samplerawPath, returnNode=True)
        [success, scapulaVolume] = slicer.util.loadSegmentation(samplescaPath, returnNode=True)
        [success, humerusVolume] = slicer.util.loadSegmentation(samplehumPath, returnNode=True)
findings.explanation: `returnNode` was removed from slicer.util load functions in current Slicer, so the registered unittest (slicer_add_python_unittest in ScapularMorphology/CMakeLists.txt:27) raises TypeError. The test also downloads sample data into the extension's Scripts folder and runs full GPU/CPU inference, so it cannot serve as a CI smoke test.
findings.suggestion: Use the current load API, keep test data in a temporary directory, and make the test skip gracefully when network or models are unavailable.

items.title: Heat/CPU defaults use 'True' but the GUI compares against 'true'

findings.title: Heat/CPU defaults use 'True' but the GUI compares against 'true'
findings.explanation: updateGUIFromParameterNode compares `GetParameter("Heat") == "true"` (lines 221-222) while the default is "True", so on a fresh scene the checkboxes do not reflect the stored state and the saved settings are not restored consistently.
findings.suggestion: Use one canonical value (e.g. "true"/"false") everywhere.

items.title: Inference script has fragile error handling and index casts

findings.title: Inference script has fragile error handling and index casts
findings.explanation: An empty slice range (e.g. scapula and humerus masks never within 25 mm, or an IS range outside the volume) aborts with a bare AssertionError instead of a user-readable message. Related: `np.int8(np.round(gc_idx))` (line 154) overflows for indices above 127 in the 512-wide crop, and `affine = ori_aff_mat` followed by in-place modification (lines 89-90) mutates the original affine metadata.
findings.suggestion: Raise a descriptive error, use int32/int64 for indices, and copy the affine before modifying it.

items.title: Input node types are inconsistent between the .ui file, the code and the parameter node defaults

findings.title: Input node types are inconsistent between the .ui file, the code and the parameter node defaults
findings.explanation: The .ui declares vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode for both inputs and the output, the code overrides them to vtkMRMLSegmentationNode (ScapularMorphology.py:103-105), and initializeParameterNode() auto-selects the first vtkMRMLScalarVolumeNode into 'ScapulaVolume'/'HumerusVolume' (lines 176-183), which the segmentation-only selectors cannot display. The masks are then written with a vtkMRMLSegmentationStorageNode to a .nrrd file (lines 488-491) and read back by MONAI LoadImage, which is unlikely to yield the single binary mask the pipeline expects.
findings.suggestion: Make the .ui, the code and the parameter-node defaults agree on segmentation nodes, and verify the written file is a binary labelmap the inference script can consume.

items.title: Landmark index cast to int8 overflows for indices above 127

findings.title: Landmark index cast to int8 overflows for indices above 127
findings.explanation: np.int8 wraps values outside -128 to 127. CT slice and voxel indices routinely exceed 127, so the glenoid index wraps to a wrong value and is passed on to cal_landmarks. The landmark index list is not written to the output in the current code, so the visible effect is limited, but the cast is wrong.
findings.suggestion: Use np.int32 or plain integers, and apply the same fix to the landmark index cast on line 194.

items.title: License and provenance of the downloaded model weights are not stated

findings.title: License and provenance of the downloaded model weights are not stated
findings.evidence: The module internally downloads pretrained model weights to intialize models.
findings.explanation: The extension code is MIT, but nothing in the repository states the terms under which model_2d.pt and model_3d.pt (and the linked training repository) may be redistributed or used, and the 2D model also initializes with `encoder_weights="imagenet"` (scapularmorphology_inference.py:103), which downloads third-party pretrained weights at runtime. Users and the index cannot tell whether the weights are research-only.
findings.suggestion: State the weights' license/provenance in the README (and in the release notes), and note any non-commercial or research-only restriction.

items.title: Long-running work blocks the GUI thread with no progress reporting

findings.title: Long-running work blocks the GUI thread with no progress reporting
findings.explanation: process() runs pip installs (line 436), the weight download (line 437) and the blocking readline loop of logProcessOutput on the GUI thread, so Slicer freezes for the whole run (minutes on first use, when pip installs and downloads happen) with only a wait cursor and no progress or cancel.
findings.suggestion: Run the pipeline in a CLI node or a worker thread with progress reporting, and separate dependency installation from the inference step.

items.title: Model weights are downloaded into the installed extension directory without confirmation

findings.title: Model weights are downloaded into the installed extension directory without confirmation
findings.evidence:
current_file_path = os.path.abspath(__file__)
        current_dir = os.path.dirname(current_file_path)
        destination_folder = os.path.join(current_dir, 'Scripts')
        model2dPath = os.path.join(destination_folder, 'model_2d.pt')
        model3dPath = os.path.join(destination_folder, 'model_3d.pt')
findings.explanation: Weights are written inside the extension installation folder, which may be read-only for system-wide installs and is deleted on extension update, forcing a re-download. The download starts automatically on the first Apply with no size/consent prompt.
findings.suggestion: Store weights in the Slicer user settings/cache directory and ask the user before downloading.

items.title: Module help text is unedited template text

findings.title: Module help text is still the template placeholder and there is no research-use disclaimer
findings.evidence: self.parent.helpText = _(""" This is an example of scripted loadable module bundled in an extension. See more information in module documentation. """)
findings.explanation: Users see template text instead of a description of the workflow, and the README gives no accuracy/validation figures or statement that the output is for research use only, which matters for a landmark/segmentation AI tool used in orthopaedic planning.
findings.suggestion: Replace the placeholder help text with the real workflow description and add a short research-use disclaimer plus validation summary.

findings.title: Module help text is unedited template text
findings.evidence: This is an example of scripted loadable module bundled in an extension. See more information in module documentation.
findings.explanation: The help text still describes the module as an example, which misleads users about what the module does and where to find documentation.
findings.suggestion: Replace it with a description of the glenoid and landmark pipeline and a link to the README tutorial.

items.title: Scalar volumes are written with the segmentation storage node

findings.title: Scalar volumes are written with the segmentation storage node
findings.explanation: processVolume creates vtkMRMLSegmentationStorageNode and uses it to write the scapula and humerus inputs, which are typed as scalar volumes. The inputs are actually segmentation nodes from the widget. The writer and the reader (MONAI LoadImage on NRRD) are not aligned, so the input array may not match what the model expects. I could not run this to confirm.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the exact NRRD layout the model expects. Write a labelmap or a scalar volume explicitly, and fix the type hints so they match what the GUI passes.

items.title: Selected output segmentation node is ignored; a new node is created on every run

findings.title: Selected output segmentation node is ignored; a new node is created on every run
findings.evidence:
def readSegmentation(self, output2DSegmentationFile):
        segNode2D = slicer.mrmlScene.AddNewNodeByClass("vtkMRMLSegmentationNode", "ScapularGlenoid")
        scavolumeStorageNode = slicer.mrmlScene.CreateNodeByClass("vtkMRMLSegmentationStorageNode")
        scavolumeStorageNode.SetFileName(output2DSegmentationFile)
        scavolumeStorageNode.ReadData(segNode2D)
findings.explanation: The `outputSegmentation` argument passed through process()/processVolume() is never used, so the node the user chose in the Outputs selector stays empty while a new 'ScapularGlenoid' node is added each click. The storage node created here is also never UnRegister()ed, leaking a node per run.
findings.suggestion: Write the result into the user-selected segmentation node (or remove the selector) and UnRegister the temporary storage node.

items.title: Test does not assert anything and downloads data from the network

findings.title: Test does not assert anything and downloads data from the network
findings.evidence:
logic.process(scapulaVolume, humerusVolume, outputSegmentation,
                            False, False, False, False)
findings.explanation: test_ScapularMorphology downloads sample data and runs logic.process, but it never checks the output. The ctest registration is commented out, so CI does not exercise the module. This gives no protection against regressions.
findings.suggestion: Assert the segmentation and landmark outputs (for example segment count and fiducial count). Register the test in CTest. Keep the test data in a fixed, checksummed location.

items.title: Catalog scm_revision is a moving branch

findings.title: Catalog scm_revision is a moving branch
findings.explanation: The catalog entry uses scm_revision "main", so the built code can change without a catalog update. The reviewed commit is 28fe666318286c72303515ba32902b51cf1864a5.
findings.suggestion: Pin scm_revision to a reviewed commit or release tag.

items.title: No license stated for the downloaded model weights and sample data

findings.title: No license stated for the downloaded model weights and sample data
findings.explanation: The MIT license covers the code. The weights and sample files are downloaded from the author's GitHub releases, and their terms are not stated in the repository. Redistribution by others is therefore uncertain.
findings.suggestion: State the terms for the model weights and sample data in the README.
